question:
A 55-year-old man with no prior medical conditions comes to the emergency department complaining
of a headache and numbness with tingling in his left arm that began 2 days ago and has since spread
to his left face and leg. Just before arrival, he also experienced clumsiness in his left hand and difficulty
walking, often veering to the left. He denies any history of recreational drug use. On physical
examination, the patient is afebrile, with a heart rate of 87 beats per minute and a blood pressure of
115/91 mm Hg. There is no tenderness of the head or spine, no neck stiffness, and no visible skin
lesions. Cardiac examination reveals no murmurs. Neurologic examination shows a left-pronator drift,
mild weakness in the left ankle dorsiflexion, and lower facial weakness on the left. Sensory testing
reveals diminished sensation to light touch, vibration, and temperature across the entire left face, arm,
and leg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Viral meningitis (B)
Intracranial tumor (C) Subdural hematoma (D) Migraine with aura (E) Brain abscess (F) Acute stroke
(G) Transient ischemic attack (H) Conversion disorder (I) Cerebral venous thrombosis (J) Viral
encephalitis
 A. Conversion disorder
B. Cerebral venous thrombosis
C. Viral meningitis
D. Acute stroke
E. Subdural hematoma
F. Intracranial tumor
G. Viral encephalitis
H. Migraine with aura
I. Brain abscess

J. Transient ischemic attack
